0.0.n: Signals that the speaker has reached understanding, with a possible hint of impatience.

0.1.n: Polite past form of 分かる, used to acknowledge that something is now understood.

0.3.n: A job title for a section manager, used here to address the boss directly.

1.0.n: A casual, masculine way to refer to yourself, even though the sentence ends politely.

1.1.n: Links 俺 to 悪行 to show whose misdeeds they are.

1.2.n: A strong word for wrongdoing, making these workplace confessions sound dramatic.

1.4.n: Combines with から to mark when the confession will begin.

1.5.n: Marks 今 as the starting point in time.

1.6.n: Shows that the speaker intends to leave none of his misdeeds out.

1.7.n: Polite form of 言う, expressing what the speaker is about to do.

2.0.n: The て-form of まとめる describes dealing with everything as one group.

2.1.n: 回 counts occurrences, so １回 limits the angry reaction to a single occasion.

2.2.n: Marks one occasion as the limit within which everything should be handled.

2.3.n: The stem of キレる, a slang verb for suddenly getting very angry.

2.4.n: Joins キレ to ください to form a request.

2.5.n: Follows a verb's て-form to ask someone to do something.

2.7.n: A polite appeal added after the request to emphasize how much the speaker wants it.

3.0.n: With も, 何回 expresses repeated occurrences rather than asking a question.

3.1.n: Turns 何回 into an expression of frequent repetition.

3.2.n: Repeating 何回も emphasizes how exhausting the repeated scolding would be.

3.3.n: Completes the second 何回も, reinforcing the repetition.

3.4.n: Part of 怒られる, the form of 怒る showing that the speaker receives the scolding.

3.5.n: In casual speech, the final る of 怒られる becomes ん before の.

3.6.n: Turns the preceding action into a thing the speaker can comment on.

3.8.n: The speaker inserts this casual masculine pronoun to identify who would lose their mind.

3.10.n: Literally means head; here it refers to the speaker's mental state.

3.11.n: The linking form of おかしい before なる describes the state someone changes into.

3.12.n: Combines with おかしく to describe a change in mental state.

3.13.n: Casual shortening of ので, giving the reason for the earlier request.

4.0.n: A casual, masculine way to refer to yourself, even though the sentence ends politely.

4.1.n: Links 俺 to 悪行 to show whose misdeeds they are.

4.2.n: A strong word for wrongdoing, making these workplace confessions sound dramatic.

4.4.n: Combines with から to mark when the confession will begin.

4.5.n: Marks 今 as the starting point in time.

4.6.n: Shows that the speaker intends to leave none of his misdeeds out.

4.7.n: Polite form of 言う, expressing what the speaker is about to do.

5.0.n: An everyday shortened loanword referring to a personal computer.

5.1.n: Adds the computer problem to the other things being confessed.

5.3.n: Emphasizes that the problem has lasted a surprisingly long time.

5.4.n: Literally half a year; it measures how far back the problem began.

5.5.n: Makes the six-month estimate approximate rather than exact.

5.6.n: After a length of time, 前 places something that far in the past.

5.7.n: Marks approximately six months ago as the beginning of the ongoing problem.

5.8.n: 動いていない loses い in speech; です makes the negative description polite.

6.0.n: A hesitation word used before making an awkward admission.

6.2.n: The thing being taken home; casual speech leaves out the object marker を.

6.3.n: Describes how regularly the speaker takes the toilet paper.

6.4.n: The て-form of 持つ combines with 帰る to express taking something home.

6.5.n: The て-form of 帰る leads into a shortened ongoing-action expression.

6.6.n: Here 帰っているの contracts to 帰ってんの, describing a repeated habit.

6.7.n: Turns the preceding action into a description of the person doing it.

6.9.n: This casual masculine pronoun identifies the speaker as the person responsible.

6.10.n: Politely completes the identification of the culprit as the speaker.

7.0.n: A job title, not a name; the speaker is referring to the boss he is addressing.

7.1.n: Connects 課長 to 悪口, identifying the target of the negative comments.

7.2.n: Refers to insulting or negative talk, not necessarily false rumors.

7.3.n: Names the people who have been hearing the negative comments.

7.4.n: Marks みんな as the recipients of what the speaker spreads.

7.5.n: The て-form of 言いふらす, which means telling something widely, often with a negative implication.

7.6.n: Here 言いふらしているの contracts to 言いふらしてんの, describing ongoing behavior.

7.7.n: Turns the preceding action into a description of the person responsible.

7.9.n: This casual masculine pronoun identifies the speaker as the person spreading the comments.

7.10.n: Adds politeness to the speaker's identification of himself.

7.11.n: At the sentence end, this stresses the admission as something the listener should take into account.

8.0.n: Signals a transition from confessing to repeating the request.

8.2.n: The て-form of まとめる asks for all the misdeeds to be handled as one group.

8.3.n: 回 counts occurrences, limiting the requested outburst to a single occasion.

8.4.n: Marks one occasion as the limit for dealing with everything.

8.5.n: The stem of キレる, a slang verb for suddenly getting very angry.

8.6.n: Joins キレ to ください to form a request.

8.7.n: Follows a verb's て-form to ask someone to do something.

8.9.n: Repeats the polite appeal as a separate sentence for extra emphasis.

9.0.n: A Japanese surname, used here to address the employee directly.

10.0.n: Acknowledges being called by name and signals readiness to listen.

11.0.n: Literally means neck, but colloquially refers to dismissal from a job.

11.1.n: The plain counterpart of です gives this declaration a blunt, forceful finish.

0.tip: 分かりました uses the polite past form to acknowledge understanding now.

1.lit: My misdeeds, from now, all I will tell.
1.tip: The object marker を is omitted after 悪行, which is common in casual speech.

2.lit: Putting them together, in one time, please lose your temper; I ask you.
2.tip: A verb's て-form plus ください makes a request, even when the verb itself is slang.

3.lit: Being scolded many times, many times, I, because my head will become strange.
3.tip: 怒られんの is a casual contraction of 怒られるの, not a negative form.

4.lit: My misdeeds, from now, all I will tell.
4.tip: 今から means starting now, while 言います expresses the speaker's intention to speak.

5.lit: The computer too, already since about half a year ago, hasn't been working.
5.tip: A time expression plus 前から means since that long ago.

6.lit: Um, the one taking toilet paper home every day is me.
6.tip: An action followed by の can mean the person doing it, as in の、俺です.

7.lit: Because the one spreading nasty comments about the manager to everyone is me.
7.tip: 課長の悪口 means negative comments about the manager, not comments made by him.

8.lit: Okay, putting them together, in one time, please lose your temper. I ask you.
8.tip: １回で asks for everything to be dealt with on one occasion.

9.tip: Using a surname alone can sound blunt or authoritative, especially from a boss.

10.tip: はい is also used to respond when someone calls your name.

11.tip: クビだ is a blunt way to announce dismissal; the person being fired is understood from context.
